## Part A. Written BEFORE the run (do not edit after the run starts)

(From the E0.9 row of EXPERIMENTS.md section 3 and the owner's addition of 2026-10-27; this file was created after the
generator measurement below, before any training measurement.)

**Gap / phase:** Phase 0 (foundations).

**Hypothesis (one sentence):** none; a measurement: points per second per GPU at 5M, whether generation is the bottleneck, and
what deterministic mode costs.

**Change (exact config diff against B0):**
```
generator version: v0, B0 (v0-b0-af75b1af)
switches: none
mix weights: B0
anything else: torch's default mode vs torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) + CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
```

**Run id(s):** gen_throughput (generator alone); 5M training throughput in T3.

**What should move:** nothing. Record:
- generator points/s at L = 1024 / 4096 / 8192, default vs deterministic (tools/gen_throughput.py);
- end-to-end 5M training points/s per GPU, default vs deterministic generator (T3);
- the same for each new family as it lands.

**Win rule:** numbers recorded. Decision rule (owner): if deterministic mode is cheap, training runs the generator in it.

**What would make this a failure:** none (a measurement).

**Cost estimate:** minutes on one A100 for the generator; T3 for training.

## Part B. Written AFTER the run

**What actually ran:** tools/gen_throughput.py on Perlmutter (compute node nid200293, A100, torch 2.13.0+cu130),
2026-10-27: generate_blocks of B0 (8 lanes, about one 16M-point generation pool per call), each mode in a fresh process,
2 warm-up calls, mean of 5 timed calls. Log: logs/perlmutter/gen_throughput.log (not committed).

**Results (generator alone):**

| L (+128 pred) | Default mode, points/s | Deterministic mode, points/s | Deterministic / default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.667e8 | 1.328e8 | 0.797 |
| 4096 | 1.641e8 | 1.319e8 | 0.804 |
| 8192 | 1.768e8 | 1.439e8 | 0.814 |

**Decision (owner, 2026-10-27):** training runs the generator in deterministic mode, so B0 and switch runs see identical data
apart from the switch. The model stays in torch's default mode; E0.7's seed spread covers model noise. End-to-end training
throughput is measured in both modes in T3 and the decision is revisited if the cost is above 10%.

**End to end (T3, 2026-10-31):** `t3.sh e09` on one A100: the 5M ab5m_cpm trainer, 300 steps (2.49B points) per generator
mode, then `tideforge.train.throughput report` (numbers as reported by the owner from that run):

| Generator mode | Training points/s per GPU | Generation share of wall time | Hours per 100B points |
|---|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 3.068e7 | 36.3% | 0.91 |
| default | 3.307e7 | 31.4% | 0.84 |

Deterministic / default = 0.928: the cost is 7.2%, under the 10% threshold set on 2026-10-27, so **training keeps the
deterministic generator**. tideforge/slurm.py now uses TRAIN_PTS_PER_S = 3.068e7 (measured) for every GPU-hour estimate,
and time limits use +15% instead of the 3x slack kept while the rate was an estimate.

**For later (not a decision):** generation takes 36% of wall time and does not overlap with the model step; if
deterministic generation could overlap with training (the deterministic flag is process-wide today), up to ~1.5x would be
possible (estimate: 1 / (1 - 0.36)).

**Verdict:** done. Deterministic generator, measured rate in the estimates.

**Counted looks at fev / TIME in this experiment:** 0
